title: Quantum computing for high energy nuclear physics
comment: 47 pages, 17 figures, Contribution to Encyclopedia of Nuclear Physics, comments are welcomed
summary: Quantum information science (QIS) offers a new set of conceptual and computational tools ideally suited to exploring the many-body, out-of-equilibrium, and real-time properties of strongly interacting quantum systems. These themes find a natural counterpart in high energy nuclear physics, whose central goal is to describe the properties of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), the theory of the strong interaction, under extreme conditions. Relevant examples range from the formation and internal structure of hadrons, to the collective and thermalization dynamics of strongly interacting QCD matter, and the properties of complex many-body scattering processes. Although tremendous progress has been made over the past decades in our understanding of QCD in the nuclear physics context, through perturbative methods, lattice QCD, and effective theory descriptions, phenomena that are intrinsically connected to real-time dynamics, highly entangled many-body evolution, or finite density regimes remain only partially accessible with existing approaches. In this article, we argue that QIS can help realize a new paradigm for addressing these open questions. With the aim of making the discussion accessible to both high energy nuclear physics and QIS audiences, we provide an overview of selected open problems in high energy nuclear physics, with emphasis on aspects motivated by collider phenomenology, and discuss how they can be approached using QIS tools. This connection is illustrated through representative examples drawn from the recent literature, making the case that QIS can become a driving force for discovery in nuclear physics in the coming years.

title: Spurious center-of-mass mode as an $S$-matrix pole within the Jost-random-phase approximation
summary: Within the Jost-random-phase approximation (Jost-RPA), the spurious center-of-mass mode is a zero of the Jost determinant and hence a pole of the $S$ matrix. A zero at zero excitation energy $E$, whether from self-consistency or from a calibration of the residual interaction, is a pole of exactly second order when it has a single independent solution, every unoccupied bound orbital lies above the holes, and each hole is paired with every allowed partial wave; the order follows from the position of the zero, not from self-consistency. The state of this double pole, given by the Autonne-Takagi factorization of its $E^{-2}$ coefficient, is the zero-energy solution normalized by its inertia. In a self-consistent model of one energy density of the neutron and proton densities, every physical $S$-matrix element continued to $E=0$ carries the $E^{-2}$ term, contrary to an earlier conclusion. Subtracting the mode's principal part from the response changes the strength at real $E\neq0$ only through the smoothing and, in such a model, coincides with the projection of the ideal spurious state. In uncalibrated Woods-Saxon models of $^{16}$O and $^{208}$Pb the mode is a pair of poles on the imaginary axis.

title: Interacting Boson System at Finite Temperatures: The treatment of the lattice QCD results
summary: We study an interacting relativistic system of charged bosons at finite temperature and fixed isospin density within a thermodynamically consistent mean-field approach. The interaction is represented by repulsive phi-4 and phi-6 self-interactions, which generate a density-dependent effective mass of the bosonic quasiparticles. We formulate the thermodynamics in the Extended Canonical Ensemble, obtained from the grand canonical description by a Legendre transformation from the isospin chemical potential to the conserved isospin density. In the condensed phase the chemical potential is constrained by the Bose-condensation condition and is therefore determined self-consistently through the effective mass. We apply the formalism to a pion-like system at finite isospin and clarify the relation between the isospin chemical-potential conventions used for pion and quark degrees of freedom. Using the convention adopted in lattice-QCD calculations, we compare the pressure, isospin density, energy density, and trace anomaly with lattice results at T=120 MeV. With one constant fitted to the lattice pressure, each model reproduces the lattice isospin density, energy density, and trace anomaly. Both the phi-4 and phi-6 models reproduce the main features of the lattice data, with the phi-6 interaction providing the better description. The Extended Canonical Ensemble provides a convenient framework for treating interacting particle-antiparticle systems across the transition to the Bose-condensed phase.

title: Multi-phonon wobbling excitations as a probe for dynamical quasiparticle alignment
summary: The multiple and very extended triaxial strongly deformed bands of the $^{163,165}$Lu nuclei are used to ascertain the spin dependence of the odd quasiparticle alignment. The band heads are found to favor a tilted alignment geometry which gradually evolves into a transverse configuration. Distinct dynamical regimes are thus identified in specific bands and spin intervals, which are discussed in terms of wobbling excitations based on the analysis of the wave functions and $E2$ transition probabilities.

title: Search for the 229Pa Parity Doublet via Internal-Conversion Spectroscopy at FRIB
summary: The radioisotope $^{229}$Pa is predicted to possess a nearly degenerate ground-state parity doublet. Previous $γ$-ray and conversion-electron spectroscopy suggests a splitting of $ΔE = (60\pm 50)~\mathrm{eV}$, although the doublet's existence remains unconfirmed. Such a small splitting would give $^{229}$Pa an exceptionally large enhancement of symmetry-violating nuclear properties. However, the splitting, and with it the sensitivity of $^{229}$Pa to CP-violating physics, remains uncertain by orders of magnitude. We propose an experiment to measure this splitting with sub-eV precision within a few days of measurement time by using delayed-coincidence internal-conversion spectroscopy of $^{229}$Pa ions produced by the electron-capture decay of $^{229}$U$^{+}$ ions stored in a Penning trap at the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB). This measurement would provide the key nuclear-structure input needed to establish $^{229}$Pa as a leading candidate for next-generation atomic and molecular electric-dipole-moment (EDM) experiments.

title: Density-driven $α$-particle clustering in neutron-rich oxygen isotopes
summary: In this work, we study the effect of valence neutrons on density-driven localisation in the neutron-rich oxygen isotopes. Calculations are performed within the multidimensionally constrained relativistic Hartree--Bogoliubov model using the DD-ME2 covariant energy-density functional. By constraining the mass rms radius to larger values, we study the structural evolution of these nuclei under progressive dilution, from spatially delocalised configurations to localised clustered states. The total energy, pairing correlations, deformation, and proton and neutron density distributions are analysed to determine how valence neutrons influence the emergence of $α$-like clustering. For all three isotopes, we find a transition from a spatially delocalised nucleonic configuration to a tetrahedral $4α$-like structure. The onset of this transition occurs at similar values of the radius-derived relative dilution parameter, $χ_{\mathrm{PT}}=ρ_{\mathrm{PT}}/ ρ_{\mathrm{GS}}\simeq 0.28$--$0.31$, and shows only a weak dependence on neutron number. The excess neutrons modify the clustered density by increasing the density in the central regions and between clusters, while leaving the underlying tetrahedral core structure largely intact. Finally, we also use a phenomenological four-centre Hückel-type mapping of nuclei, which provides a molecular-orbital-like interpretation of cluster structures. We find that the effective coupling between the cluster centers decreases by progressively expanding the nucleus. The centroid-referenced energy shift $ΔE_{\mathrm{val}}$ also becomes less negative and provides smaller net molecular-orbital-like energy lowering relative to its centroid with increasing neutron number.

title: New Neutron Polarizabilities from Deuterium Compton Scattering at HI$γ$S
summary: Elastic and inelastic Compton-scattering cross sections of the deuteron were measured at HI$γ$S using a circularly polarized, quasi-monoenergetic $γ$-ray beam (61.0 MeV). Scattered $γ$ rays from a liquid deuterium target were detected at $55^\circ$, $115^\circ$, and $150^\circ$. High-resolution NaI(Tl) detectors at backward angles enabled separation of elastic and inelastic events. A $χ$EFT analysis of the data yields new neutron scalar polarizabilities, $α^n_{E1} = 12.25 \pm 1.1\mathrm{(stat)} \pm 0.3\mathrm{(BSR)} \pm 0.8\mathrm{(th)}$ and $β^n_{M1} = 2.95 \mp 1.1\mathrm{(stat)} \mp 0.3\mathrm{(BSR)} \mp 0.8\mathrm{(th)}$ (in units of $10^{-4} \mathrm{fm}^3$) reducing statistical uncertainties by 12 %.
